raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #48150. `fused_marlin_moe` never reads `--enable-deterministic-inference`, so a MoE model on the Marlin runner gives different bits for identical calls with the flag on. Two sources vary between calls:

- atomic-add reductions in the Marlin GEMM, which decide the result at decode sizes;
- the order in which `moe_align_block_size` places each expert's entries, which decides which entries share a GEMM block at prefill sizes.

#26627 turns off the atomic adds under the flag for Kimi-K2.5. This PR includes that and adds the entry order, which is the larger source at prefill sizes on current main (ablation below). It reads the flag through `get_exec()`, since `get_global_server_args()` has been retired. #26627's dual-stream change in `deepseek_v2.py` is a separate concern and isn't included here. If maintainers would rather land this through #26627, I'm happy to close this one.

## Modifications

- `fused_marlin_moe.py`: under the flag, `use_atomic_add` is false, and after `moe_align_block_size` each expert's entries are sorted ascending with padding last (`_order_entries_within_experts`).
  - The sort keys on runs of equal block expert ids instead of the ids themselves, so it doesn't depend on `expert_ids` being sorted (the expert-parallel path doesn't certify that). It handles the `-1` blocks and the `[padded_tokens, inactive_blocks]` count from #45462.
  - Tensor ops only (`cumsum`, gather, stable `argsort`), so CUDA graphs capture it.
  - The single-token `moe_align_single_token` path isn't sorted: its top-k ids are distinct, so each expert holds one entry.
- `test_moe_wna16_marlin.py` and the manual `bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py` call `fused_marlin_moe` without a server. `get_exec()` raises when no config is published, so both now publish a dummy config, as `test_marlin_moe.py` already does.
- `test_marlin_moe.py`: `test_fused_marlin_moe_deterministic_inference_repeats_bitwise`. Int4 GPTQ weights in fp16, with and without expert parallelism (dispatcher-style local ids, `-1` for non-local experts). It checks that five calls under the flag match to the bit and that the result matches the default path within `1e-3`.

Nothing changes with the flag off.

## Accuracy Tests

Kernel level, on an RTX 5060 Ti (SM120), torch 2.14.1+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.10. The NVFP4 case is the issue's shape (random weights through `prepare_moe_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin`, 256 experts, hidden 4096, width 1024, top-6, bf16). Counts are calls identical to the first, out of 10:

| Case | Flag off | Flag on | Max abs difference, flag on vs off |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| NVFP4, 1 token | 0 | 10 | 0.0625 (one bf16 step at that magnitude) |
| NVFP4, 512 tokens | 0 | 10 | 0.0625 |
| NVFP4, 2,700 tokens | 0 | 10 | 0.0625 |
| int4 fp16, 512 tokens, 64 experts | 0 | 10 | 1.5e-5 |
| int4 fp16, 512 tokens, expert parallel (8 of 16 local) | 0 | 10 | 1.5e-5 |

Ablation on current main, flag on, identical out of 10:

| Case | Atomic adds off only | Entry sort only | Both |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NVFP4, 512 tokens | 5 | 10 | 10 |
| NVFP4, 2,700 tokens | 1 | 10 | 10 |
| int4 fp16, 256 tokens | 0 | 10 | 10 |

At 1 token, the single-token path doesn't sort, and turning off atomic adds takes it from 0/10 to 10/10.

A CUDA graph captured with the flag on replays identically to eager (5 of 5).

I didn't run a server-level eval; the issue reports the server-level effect (TP2/TP4, 48 of 48 identical pairs) for the equivalent change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`marker.do_bench` with CUDA graphs, same NVFP4 shapes and GPU. The weights (~1.6 GB) far exceed L2 (32 MB), so argument cloning is skipped. Times are per `fused_marlin_moe` call:

| Tokens | Flag off | Flag on | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 114 us | 116 us | +2.0% |
| 64 | 3.41 ms | 3.47 ms | +1.6% |
| 512 | 5.19 ms | 5.29 ms | +2.0% |
| 2,700 | 13.8 ms | 14.0 ms | +1.2% |

Only runs with `--enable-deterministic-inference` pay this.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing change beyond the flag doing what it says.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Validation:

- The new test fails on unmodified main (both subtests) and passes with the change, 3 of 3 runs.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_marlin_moe.py`: 4 passed, 684 subtests passed.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_moe_wna16_marlin.py`: 36 passed, 31 skipped (cases that need SM90 skip on this GPU). Without the dummy config, 4 of its `fused_marlin_moe` tests fail with `config namespace 'exec' not published`.
- `pre-commit run` on the four changed files passes.
- Tested on one RTX 5060 Ti only; not on Hopper, Blackwell datacenter GPUs or multi-GPU TP.

+def _order_entries_within_experts(
+    sorted_token_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    expert_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    num_tokens_post_padded: torch.Tensor,
+    block_size_m: int,
+    num_entries: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    num_slots = min(expert_ids.numel() * block_size_m, sorted_token_ids.numel())
+    entries = sorted_token_ids[:num_slots].to(torch.int64)
+    slots = torch.arange(num_slots, device=entries.device)
+    # An expert's blocks are contiguous, so a run of equal block ids is one expert;
+    # keying on runs instead of ids also holds when expert ids are not sorted.
+    block_runs = torch.cat(
+        [
+            expert_ids.new_zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64),
+            torch.cumsum(expert_ids[1:] != expert_ids[:-1], dim=0),
+        ]
+    )
+    # Entry ids run to num_entries, the padding sentinel; slots past the padded
+    # total keep their place after every expert.
+    key_stride = num_entries + 1
+    keys = torch.where(
+        slots < num_tokens_post_padded[0],
+        block_runs[slots // block_size_m] * key_stride + entries,
+        expert_ids.numel() * key_stride + slots,
+    )
+    ordered = sorted_token_ids.clone()
+    ordered[:num_slots] = entries[torch.argsort(keys, stable=True)].to(
+        sorted_token_ids.dtype
+    )
+    return ordered
+

+    def test_fused_marlin_moe_deterministic_inference_repeats_bitwise(self):
+        """Under --enable-deterministic-inference, repeated calls on one input match
+        to the bit, with and without expert parallelism, and still match the default path."""
+        n, k, e, topk = 256, 512, 16, 4
+        dtype = torch.half
+        quant_type = scalar_types.uint4b8
+        for expert_parallel, m in ((False, 256), (True, 512)):
+            with self.subTest(expert_parallel=expert_parallel):
+                torch.manual_seed(0)
+                local_e = e // 2 if expert_parallel else e
+                qweights, scales = [], []
+                for rows, cols in ((2 * n, k), (k, n)):
+                    w = (
+                        torch.randn((local_e, rows, cols), device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+                        / 20
+                    )
+                    quantized = [
+                        marlin_quantize(
+                            w[i].transpose(1, 0),
+                            quant_type,
+                            128,
+                            False,
+                            torch.randperm(cols),
+                        )
+                        for i in range(local_e)
+                    ]
+                    qweights.append(
+                        stack_and_dev([q[1] for q in quantized]).contiguous()
+                    )
+                    scales.append(stack_and_dev([q[2] for q in quantized]))
+
+                a = torch.randn((m, k), device="cuda", dtype=dtype) / 10
+                score = torch.randn((m, e), device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+                from sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk import fused_topk_torch_native
+
+                topk_weights, topk_ids = fused_topk_torch_native(a, score, topk, False)
+                e_map = None
+                if expert_parallel:
+                    e_map = torch.full((e,), -1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+                    e_map[:local_e] = torch.arange(
+                        local_e, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+                    )
+                    # The standard dispatcher passes local ids, -1 for non-local experts.
+                    topk_ids = e_map[topk_ids]
+                topk_ids = topk_ids.to(torch.int32)
+
+                def run():
+                    return fused_marlin_moe(
+                        a,
+                        qweights[0],
+                        qweights[1],
+                        scales[0],
+                        scales[1],
+                        score,
+                        topk_weights,
+                        topk_ids,
+                        global_num_experts=e,
+                        expert_map=e_map,
+                        num_bits=4,
+                        is_k_full=True,
+                    )
+
+                default_output = run()
+                with get_exec().deterministic.override(
+                    enable_deterministic_inference=True
+                ):
+                    outputs = [run() for _ in range(5)]
+
+                for output in outputs[1:]:
+                    self.assertTrue(torch.equal(output, outputs[0]))
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    outputs[0], default_output, atol=1e-3, rtol=0
+                )
+
